bull.b: Rapid growth across orders, marketplace volume, and revenue shows continued consumer and merchant adoption at meaningful scale. Broad momentum in restaurants, grocery, and retail can reinforce network effects, improve delivery density, and expand the platform’s long-term earnings opportunity.

The shift to sustained profitability alongside substantial operating and free cash flow strengthens DoorDash’s ability to fund product investment, infrastructure, and strategic initiatives internally. Strong cash conversion also provides resilience as the company expands beyond restaurants and integrates new capabilities.

Higher order frequency, larger baskets, and record paid subscriptions indicate improving customer engagement rather than reliance only on new-user growth. Product and technology improvements can deepen merchant and consumer retention, strengthen network effects, and support durable marketplace economics.

bear.b: The sharp increase in debt raises financial obligations just as DoorDash prepares for a large cash-and-stock acquisition. Although leverage remains moderate relative to equity, higher borrowing increases refinancing and execution risk and makes sustained cash generation more important.

Lower trailing net margin suggests that growth is not translating fully into incremental bottom-line profitability at present. If this pressure persists, it could constrain reinvestment capacity and weaken the financial cushion needed to absorb integration costs or fund expansion.

The proposed Instacart combination could broaden DoorDash’s capabilities, but its benefits depend on approvals and successful integration over an extended timetable. Regulatory conditions, operating two technology stacks, and required investment create execution uncertainty before projected synergies can be realized.
